note: Rows the main session added after the agent sweeps. From data/research/datacenter_bills.json, with duplicates of held events dropped.

events.title: Reps. Evans and Castor introduce the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)
events.summary: H.R. 9340 would add a PURPA 111(d) standard for large loads of 100 MW or more: full incremental upgrade costs recovered from the customer, with financial assurances. Referred to Energy and Commerce.
events.significance: A bipartisan House bill that sets a consider-and-decide standard for states rather than a binding federal rule.

sources.title: H.R. 9340 (IH) text

events.title: Sen. Husted introduces Senate companion S. 5028
events.summary: Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) introduced S. 5028, the Senate version of the Ratepayer Protection Act. Referred to Energy and Natural Resources.
events.significance: Gave the House bill a Senate vehicle; Husted is in a competitive Ohio race where data centers are an issue.

sources.title: S. 5028 (IS) text

events.title: House Energy and Commerce approves Ratepayer Protection Act 52-0, narrowed to data centers
events.summary: Committee adopted an Evans substitute by voice vote that limited the definition to data centers at 100 MW or more, then approved the bill 52-0. The Data Center Coalition objected that the change singled out data centers; steel and industrial customer groups backed it.
events.significance: Shows the fight over whether large-load rules should cover all big users or only data centers.

sources.title: House committee narrows data center energy bill
Data center lobby grumbles about reworked Ratepayer Protection Act
House Energy and Commerce Advances Energy Bills ... Ratepayer Protection Act Clears 52-0

events.title: Energy and Commerce reports H.R. 9340 (H. Rept. 119-814)
events.summary: The reported version carries the data-center-only definition and added cosponsors.
events.significance: Clears the bill for a House floor vote.

sources.title: H.R. 9340 (RH) text

events.title: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the GRID Act (S. 3852)
events.summary: Bill would require data centers of 20 MW or more to run off the grid within 180 days, give existing sites 10 years via annual Zero Rate Effect Certificates, and set public reporting rules.
events.significance: First bipartisan Senate bill on data center electricity costs this Congress, per E&E News; takes the off-grid route rather than cost allocation.

sources.title: S. 3852 (IS) text
Hawley, Blumenthal Introduce Bill to Prevent Data Centers from Increasing Electricity Costs for Americans

events.title: Van Hollen introduces Power for the People Act (S. 3682)
events.summary: Bill would have FERC require data center load queues and local transmission cost allocation, and have states consider data-center rate classes. Eight Democratic cosponsors.
events.significance: The most detailed Democratic data center cost bill; combines FERC and state levers.

sources.title: S. 3682 (IS) text
Van Hollen Leads New Bill to Ensure Americans Aren't Footing the Bill for Big Data Centers

events.title: Tonko introduces House companion H.R. 8241
events.summary: Rep. Paul Tonko introduced the House version of the Power for the People Act with Rep. Kathy Castor and others.
events.significance: Castor co-leads the Republican-led Ratepayer Protection Act and is also on this stronger Democratic bill.

sources.title: H.R. 8241 (IH) text

events.title: Heinrich introduces GRID Savings Act (S. 5199)
events.summary: Bill would add Federal Power Act section 224, giving FERC jurisdiction over interconnection of loads of 150 MW or more and requiring a final rule within a year that assigns interconnection and direct-assignment costs to the large load and requires financial security.
events.significance: Democratic ENR ranking member's answer to the Ratepayer Protection Pledge; reopens whether FERC controls large-load interconnection.

sources.title: Heinrich Introduces Legislation to Ensure Large Users of Electricity Pay for Grid Upgrades
One Senate Democrat's answer to Trump's 'ratepayer protection pledge'
S. 5199 (IS) text

events.title: Heinrich blocks Ratepayer Protection Act by unanimous consent; Moreno blocks Heinrich's GRID Savings Act request
events.summary: Heinrich said the Husted bill falls short and asked to pass his GRID Savings Act instead. Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) objected.
events.significance: Both parties' lead bills were blocked on the same day, each side calling the other's version inadequate.

sources.title: Senate Democrat blocks House-passed bill to shield Americans from data center energy costs, proposing alternate measure

events.title: Menendez and Casar introduce Data Center Transparency Act (H.R. 6984)
events.summary: Would require EIA to collect data center energy use every 6 months and EPA to report quarterly on water and emissions.
events.significance: The EIA data-collection model also appears in BAAJA section 2114 and the Clean Cloud Act.

sources.title: H.R. 6984 (IH) text

events.title: Rep. Donalds introduces Protecting Ratepayers Act (H.R. 9777)
events.summary: Would bar new and existing data centers of 5 MW or more from using the grid or public water and would give the Ratepayer Protection Pledge proclamation the force of law.
events.significance: A Republican off-grid bill that goes further than the Ratepayer Protection Act; Donalds is running for Florida governor.

sources.title: H.R. 9777 (IH) text
Byron Donalds, running for Florida governor, announces data center legislation

events.title: Blunt Rochester and Curtis introduce Senate Data Center Transparency Act and Community Empowerment Act
events.summary: Senate version of the transparency bill, plus a DOE technical-assistance program for communities. House companion led by Rep. Menendez.
events.significance: Bipartisan Senate push for data center energy, water and environmental reporting.

sources.title: Senators Blunt Rochester, Curtis Introduce Bills to Help Public Understand Impacts of Data Centers

events.title: Seven hyperscalers sign White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge
events.summary: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and xAI signed. President Trump issued a proclamation saying the Pledge effectuates national policy. The Federal Register published it on 2026-03-09 (91 FR 11439).
events.significance: The voluntary baseline that H.R. 9340 would partly codify and H.R. 9777 would make law.

sources.title: Ratepayer Protection Pledge
Ratepayer Protection Pledge Proclamation
Ratepayer Protection Pledge

events.title: State ratepayer advocates say FERC's PJM show cause order leaves data center transmission costs with other customers
events.summary: Advocates from Delaware, Illinois, Maryland, Ohio and Pennsylvania filed at FERC, arguing the order does not fix cost allocation of network upgrades for large loads.
events.significance: Shows the gap between FERC's June process and the full-cost standard in the bills.
actors: Delaware, Illinois, Maryland and Ohio ratepayer advocates

sources.title: FERC fails to shield PJM consumers from data center transmission costs: ratepayer advocates

events.title: Six grid operators file large-load informational reports at FERC
events.summary: Each RTO/ISO described its plan for resource adequacy for large loads, a first step under the June 18 show cause orders. Substantive responses were due August 17.
events.significance: Regional answers rather than a national rule.

sources.title: RTOs and ISOs Answer: A National Preview of How All Six Grid Operators Plan to Respond to the Large Load Surge

events.title: Trump expands Ratepayer Protection Pledge to governors, legislators, developers and power providers
events.summary: At EPA headquarters, the President announced the expansion; EPA says the Pledge will cover 80 percent of power delivered to homes and businesses.
events.significance: Extends the voluntary approach beyond the hyperscalers to the parties that set rates and approve projects.

sources.title: President Trump Expands Historic Ratepayer Protection Pledge to Protect American Ratepayers, Lower Electricity Prices

events.title: FERC accepts but suspends PJM reliability backstop procurement for five months
events.summary: FERC found cost allocation, transmission owner exit rules and load-serving entity collateral may be unjust and unreasonable and suggested fixes. New effective date 2027-02-28. PJM pulled its 2026-09-30 auction.
events.significance: A capacity fix driven by data center demand; FERC pressed that costs go to the customers who drive the need.

sources.title: FERC Suspends PJM's Backstop Procurement Five Months and PJM Pulls Its September 30 Auction
FERC chair slams PJM 'mess' as country's largest grid operator delays power auction
FERC Accepts PJM Reliability Backstop Proposal

events.title: Lee's push to overhaul the National Historic Preservation Act becomes a sticking point in permitting talks
events.summary: E&E News reported that Lee wanted to change the National Historic Preservation Act to speed energy projects on federal land, prioritizing limits on lawsuits. Some Democrats were wary because the law matters to tribes and preservation groups. Heinrich said he wanted to keep the law's intent while making reviews more predictable.
events.significance: Brought a law not covered by the SPEED Act or the 2024 Manchin-Barrasso bill into the Senate talks, and threatened the goal of progress before the August recess.

sources.title: Debate over preservation law tripping up permitting talks

events.title: Cortez Masto and Cotton release Senate FREEDOM Act on permit certainty
events.summary: Sens. Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) released a Senate version of the FREEDOM Act. It would keep future presidents from interfering with permitted energy projects. Unlike the House bill it drops the de-risking compensation program, lets a court appoint a contractor to finish a stalled permit, and covers projects on the Outer Continental Shelf.
events.significance: A direct precursor to the permit-certainty sections (1401 to 1403) of the final bill, which add money damages the Senate FREEDOM Act left out.

sources.title: Freedom (It Won't Slow You Down)

events.title: Nearly 60 groups urge Senate EPW not to limit state and tribal Section 401 reviews
events.summary: National and regional groups sent a letter to the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee opposing limits on state and tribal review of water quality impacts under Clean Water Act Section 401. Republicans and the administration say blue states have used Section 401 to slow or block energy projects.
events.significance: Showed organized opposition to a top Republican priority before text was released.

sources.title: Groups urge lawmakers to protect state water reviews in permitting talks

events.title: Heinrich introduces connect-and-manage interconnection bill
events.summary: Heinrich introduced a bill that lets new power plants of any type opt into a faster safety study and 'basic access service for energy-only delivery,' as Texas does, instead of waiting for full interconnection studies and paying for network upgrades. Plants would curtail output when the grid is congested.
events.significance: Heatmap read it as a sign that ranking Democrats were advancing technology-neutral grid bills that could slot into the bipartisan package.

sources.title: Scoop: A Key Democrat Wants to Break America's Worst Energy Bottleneck

events.title: Capito and Whitehouse say permitting talks are in their final stages
events.summary: Capito said a deal was very close and Whitehouse said talks were in final wrap-up, with the hardest issues resolved last. Capito said a floor vote could slip into the third week of the work session, later than the timeline she and Thune had set.
events.significance: Marked the point at which negotiators publicly expected a vote before the November elections.

sources.title: Permitting talks reach 'final' stages

events.title: Trump tells advisers he will direct Defense to clear its wind queue to close a permitting deal
events.summary: POLITICO Pro reported that Trump told Burgum, Wright and other advisers on Sept. 21 he would direct the Defense Department to start clearing its queue of delayed onshore wind projects to strike a deal. Thune had set a Tuesday deadline for a deal. Heatmap reported on Sept. 25 that Wright would not confirm the report, and that the White House had signaled the concession might lapse after November.
events.significance: The administration's treatment of wind and solar was Democrats' stated condition for a deal. The report shows the concession was offered but not locked in.

sources.title: Trump will green-light wind energy projects to strike permitting deal
Offshore Wind's Existential Crisis at Climate Week

events.title: Huffman says most House Democrats oppose the Senate permitting deal as written
events.summary: House Natural Resources ranking member Jared Huffman said most House Democrats will not back the Senate bill as written. He urged resuming talks after the midterms, expecting a better negotiating position. POLITICO reported that Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie had not endorsed it either.
events.significance: The first sign of trouble in the House for the Senate package.

sources.title: Senate bipartisan permitting deal faces a House buzz saw

events.title: Whitehouse says it makes little sense to pursue permitting reform if the administration won't faithfully execute it
events.summary: At an EPW hearing, Whitehouse called the administration's attacks on wind and solar 'gangster Gong Show stuff' and asked why Democrats would negotiate on permitting while it ignored congressional mandates. He cited Revolution Wind, the Energy Department's project kill list and a revoked Nevada solar approval.
events.significance: Set out, two months before talks formally stopped, the condition that became central to the 2026 deal: assurances on how permits would be treated.

sources.title: Whitehouse threatens to blow up permitting talks

events.title: House members introduce FREEDOM Act to bar presidents from revoking permits
events.summary: Reps. Josh Harder, Adam Gray, Mike Lawler, Don Bacon and Chuck Edwards introduced the 77-page FREEDOM Act. It would bar agencies from terminating or revoking a fully permitted project except to prevent clear and immediate harm, and set up a De-Risking Compensation Fund.
events.significance: A direct model for the permit-certainty sections of the final Senate bill. It followed the December 2025 offshore wind stop-work orders.

sources.title: Scoop: New Bipartisan House Bill Would Keep President From Yanking Permits

events.title: Administration does not appeal ruling against the Revolution Wind stop-work order
events.summary: The Justice Department let its deadline pass without appealing a federal injunction against Interior's order to stop work on Revolution Wind. Whitehouse had said any appeal would be inconsistent with progress on permitting reform; the White House said it looked forward to ultimate victory on the issue.
events.significance: Read as a sign that the administration wanted the permitting talks to continue.

sources.title: Permitting talks live on as DOJ declines to appeal ruling favoring Revolution Wind

events.title: Wright dines with Republican lawmakers on permitting after a dinner of the four Senate negotiators
events.summary: A Monday dinner organized by Sen. Hickenlooper brought together Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich; on Tuesday Energy Secretary Chris Wright dined with Republican lawmakers. Whitehouse said Democrats would hold an internal caucus vote before moving any bill.
events.significance: Showed the executive branch and Senate leaders working in parallel in May on a summer target for a deal.

sources.title: Wright meets with Republicans on permitting, but deal remains elusive as ever

events.title: Capito and Whitehouse tell the White House at POLITICO's Energy Summit to stop attacking renewables
events.summary: Both EPW leaders said the administration's moves against offshore wind and clean energy approvals put a permitting deal at risk. Whitehouse said it was hard to ask his caucus to trust the administration. The White House energy council's director said Democrats were blocking gas pipelines.
events.significance: A bipartisan message to the White House that the wind and solar holds were the main obstacle.

sources.title: Special edition: POLITICO's Energy Summit kicks off hot permitting summer

events.title: Senate Armed Services releases NDAA with King amendment on Pentagon wind reviews
events.summary: The committee released its fiscal 2027 defense bill with an amendment by Sen. Angus King to curb the Pentagon's delay in processing wind project permits. Chair Roger Wicker said the dispute needed to be resolved and that there was bipartisan support.
events.significance: A Republican-chaired committee moved to check the Defense Department's hold on onshore wind reviews, one of the Democrats' stated obstacles to a permitting deal.

sources.title: Senate releases NDAA with permitting amendment

events.title: EPA proposes changes to its NEPA procedures
events.summary: EPA proposed to conform its NEPA procedures to the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act (two-year, 150-page limits on impact statements), add the 2025 fee for expedited reviews, and apply last year's Supreme Court ruling narrowing the scope of review.
events.significance: Another agency NEPA rule written after CEQ removed its regulations; the Senate bill would write many of the same limits into statute.

sources.title: EPA floats changes to NEPA implementation rules

events.title: Pallone calls for a national data center moratorium
events.summary: Energy and Commerce ranking member Frank Pallone called for a nationwide moratorium on new data centers, saying the bills before the committee were 'not nearly enough.' Castor did not support a moratorium; Chair Guthrie's office called it 'not the answer.' AOC formally introduced a moratorium bill.
events.significance: Split House Democrats on data center policy the day of the Ratepayer Protection Act markup.

sources.title: Data center energy bill hits speed bump

events.title: EPA draft rule would end federal public-notice requirement for minor New Source Review permits
events.summary: EPA's draft rule would no longer require states and tribes to give notice and take comment before permitting 'minor' pollution sources. Advocates said it could let states permit data centers and power plants without informing nearby communities.
events.significance: An administration permitting change affecting data center siting, outside the bill's scope.

sources.title: EPA proposal could sideline the public on data center permits

events.title: Republicans reported to have made a broad permitting offer to Democrats before the July Fourth recess
events.summary: E&E News reported on July 13, citing a Democrat close to the talks, that Republicans made a broad offer before the recess covering faster environmental and historic preservation reviews, some transmission permitting and GOP priorities. Democrats were reviewing it and pressing for transmission measures and limits on canceling approved permits.
events.significance: Shows what the Republican side put on the table and what Democrats wanted in return in July.

sources.title: Where the permitting talks stand

events.title: Negotiators move their permitting deal target to September
events.summary: After a Tuesday meeting of Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich, Whitehouse said negotiators were aiming for September, when the Senate returns from a five-week recess.
events.significance: The August recess target was missed; the deal slipped into the pre-election weeks.

sources.title: It's official: Permitting deal won't happen this week

events.title: Oregon federal judge temporarily orders Pentagon to complete stalled onshore wind reviews
events.summary: A federal judge in Oregon granted renewable energy groups' motion to temporarily force the Defense Department to finish its reviews of stalled onshore wind projects. Heatmap reported on Aug. 6 that Judge Karin Immergut had said at an Aug. 4 hearing there was strong evidence the government broke statutory and regulatory deadlines.
events.significance: A court order on one of Democrats' named obstacles to a deal, though negotiators said they needed proof the administration was changing behavior on its own.

sources.title: Senators outline future of permitting talks
Trump May Be Forced to Resume Wind Project Permits

events.title: Wind developers tell the Oregon court the Pentagon can clear projects as part of the permitting deal
events.summary: In the Oregon case over the Defense Department's hold on wind airspace reviews, developers filed a response saying that if the Pentagon could approve projects with mitigation agreements awaiting countersignature in a permitting deal, it was unclear why it could not approve them to comply with the court's order.
events.significance: Developers used the administration's offer of project approvals in the talks as evidence in court that the freeze was extra-legal; Heatmap says it is unclear the bill would end the Pentagon slowdown.

sources.title: The Senate's Big Bipartisan Permitting Deal, Explained

events.title: Senate schedules a November 9 cloture vote to take up the permitting bill
events.summary: The Senate's floor schedule set its first vote after the election: cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act, which the Senate Press Gallery describes as the legislative vehicle for the permitting reform bill. The vote is set for about 5:30 p.m. on Monday, November 9.
events.significance: Makes the permitting bill the Senate's first order of business when it returns after the November 3 election.

sources.title: Thursday, October 1, 2026

events.title: More than 200 environmental and local groups ask Democratic leaders to hold the bill until next Congress
events.summary: A letter to Schumer and Jeffries, published by Punchbowl News, argues the environmental cost of the rollbacks outweighs the emissions benefits and that a better package is likely after the midterms. Signers include the Center for Biological Diversity, Food & Water Watch, Friends of the Earth Action and Greenpeace USA.
events.significance: The large national groups (NRDC, EDF, the League of Conservation Voters, Earthjustice and the national Sierra Club) did not sign, which left the environmental opposition split.

sources.title: Broad Environmental Coalition Urges Opposition to Permitting Reform Package
